name: Andhra Pradesh
description: Known as the 'Rice Bowl of India' and home to the sacred Seven Hills of Tirumala, Andhra Pradesh boasts the second longest coastline in India, deep gorges at Gandikota, and profound ancient Buddhist heritage at Amaravati.
history: Ruled by the illustrious Satavahanas (who patronized Amaravati Buddhist art), Eastern Chalukyas, Kakatiyas, and the imperial Vijayanagara Empire. Sri Krishnadevaraya's golden reign championed Telugu literature and grand temple construction.
geography: Extends from the Coromandel Coast along the Bay of Bengal through fertile Krishna and Godavari deltas to the Eastern Ghats hill tracts (Araku Valley) and semi-arid Rayalaseema plateau.
climate: Tropical climate influenced by both southwest and northeast monsoons. Coastal regions remain warm and humid; Rayalaseema is drier. Winters (November to February) are mild (16°C - 28°C).

historical_timeline.title: Satavahana Golden Era at Amaravati
historical_timeline.description: Satavahana rulers patronized Mahayana Buddhist stupas and exquisite marble limestone sculptures.
historical_timeline.significance: Center of international Buddhist pilgrimage visited by Acharya Nagarjuna.

historical_timeline.title: Peak of Vijayanagara Empire
historical_timeline.description: Emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya patronized grand gopurams at Tirupati, Srisailam, and Lepakshi.
historical_timeline.significance: Architectural and literary zenith of South Indian classical heritage.

historical_timeline.title: Formation of Andhra State
historical_timeline.description: First state carved on a linguistic basis in independent India following Potti Sreeramulu's historic fast.
historical_timeline.significance: Foundational precedent for linguistic reorganization of Indian states.

travel_transport.connectivity_tip: High-frequency rail corridors connect Vijayawada to Chennai, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru.

destinations.name: Tirupati
destinations.description: World-famous spiritual town home to the sacred hilltop Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple on Tirumala Hills.
destinations.why_famous: One of the most visited pilgrimage destinations on earth, celebrated for Dravidian architecture and sacred Tirupati Laddoos.

destinations.name: Gandikota
destinations.description: Known as the 'Grand Canyon of India', where the Pennar River cuts dramatically through rugged Erramala red granite bedrock.
destinations.why_famous: Spectacular canyon panoramas alongside the medieval 13th-century Gandikota Fort complex.

destinations.name: Araku Valley
destinations.description: Scenic Eastern Ghats hill valley known for aromatic organic coffee plantations, misty waterfalls, and million-year-old Borra Caves.
destinations.why_famous: Glass-domed Vistadome train journey through 58 tunnels and lush green deciduous mountain landscapes.

name: Arunachal Pradesh
languages: English, Nyishi, Adi, Apatani, Monpa, Hindi
description: The 'Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains', India's easternmost frontier where the sun first rises. Blessed with snow-capped Himalayan peaks, ancient Buddhist gompas in Tawang, and biodiversity-rich river valleys.
history: Anciently known in regional epics as the hermitage of sage Parashuram and the kingdom of Bhismaka. Tawang Monastery was founded in 1680-1681 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso in accordance with the wishes of the 5th Dalai Lama.
geography: Rugged Eastern Himalayas rising from 100m in the foothills to over 7,000m on the Kangto and Namcha Barwa ridgelines, drained by the Siang, Kameng, Subansiri, Dibang, and Lohit rivers.
climate: Alpine in high mountains, temperate in middle valleys, and subtropical in foothills. Summers (April to June) are pleasant. Monsoons bring heavy downpours. Winters (November to March) bring heavy snow to Tawang and Sela Pass.

historical_timeline.title: Founding of Tawang Monastery
historical_timeline.description: Merak Lama established Galden Namgey Lhatse, India's largest Buddhist monastery.
historical_timeline.significance: Major seat of Mahayana Tibetan Buddhist learning and birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama.

historical_timeline.title: The McMahon Line Agreement
historical_timeline.description: Border alignment negotiated at the Simla Convention defining the boundary between British India and Tibet.
historical_timeline.significance: Recognized international frontier for Arunachal Pradesh.

rail_hubs: Naharlagun Railway Station (direct connection to New Delhi and Guwahati)
travel_transport.connectivity_tip: Domestic travelers require an Inner Line Permit (ILP); foreign tourists require a Protected Area Permit (PAP).

destinations.name: Tawang
destinations.description: Dramatic high-altitude fortress town perched at 3,048m, housing India's largest monastery and panoramic Himalayan vistas.
destinations.why_famous: 400-year-old Tawang Monastery, sacred high-altitude Madhuri Lake, and heroic Jaswant Garh War Memorial.

destinations.name: Ziro Valley
destinations.description: UNESCO World Heritage tentative pine-clad valley inhabited by the unique Apatani tribe known for sustainable paddy-cum-fish farming.
destinations.why_famous: Apatani tribal customs, picturesque green paddy landscape, and the annual outdoor Ziro Festival of Music.

name: Chhattisgarh
description: The green forested heartland of Central India, acclaimed for the mighty horseshoe Chitrakote Falls (the 'Niagara of India'), 44% dense forest cover, vibrant tribal cultures of Bastar, and ancient temples at Sirpur.
history: Anciently known as Dakshina Kosala with its capital at Sirpur. Ruled by the Sarabhapuriyas, Somavamshis, Kalachuris of Ratanpur, and the Kakatiya rulers of Bastar. Deeply linked to Rama's exile path (Ram Van Gaman Path).
geography: Encompasses the fertile central plains of the Mahanadi river basin, flanked by northern Maikal Hills (Satpura range) and the forested plateau of Bastar and Dandakaranya in the south.
climate: Tropical wet and dry climate. Pleasant winters (November to February, 12°C - 26°C); hot summers (April to June, up to 43°C); southwest monsoon rains from July to September.

historical_timeline.title: Golden Age of Sirpur
historical_timeline.description: Queen Vasata built the monumental brick Lakshmana Temple, one of India's finest terracotta monuments.
historical_timeline.significance: Center of harmonious co-existence of Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu architecture.

historical_timeline.title: Establishment of Bastar Kingdom
historical_timeline.description: King Annama Deva of the Kakatiya lineage established the Bastar kingdom under the patronage of Goddess Danteshwari.
historical_timeline.significance: Preserved unique indigenous tribal governance and the historic 75-day Bastar Dussehra festival.

travel_transport.connectivity_tip: Raipur is a major railway junction with direct Superfast connectivity to Mumbai, Delhi, Howrah, and Chennai.

destinations.name: Chitrakote Falls
destinations.description: Magnificent 300-meter-wide horseshoe waterfall on the Indravati River, famed as the 'Niagara of India'.
destinations.why_famous: India's widest natural waterfall with dramatic roaring cascades, boat rides up to the mist, and nighttime illumination.

destinations.name: Bastar
destinations.description: Cultural soul of Chhattisgarh famous for tribal art villages, Kanger Valley National Park, and Kotumsar limestone stalactite caves.
destinations.why_famous: Dhokra bell-metal craft, ancient Danteshwari Temple, and vibrant weekly haats (tribal village markets).

name: Goa
description: India's premier sunshine state on the Arabian Sea, renowned for pristine palm-fringed golden beaches, 450 years of Portuguese baroque architecture, UNESCO heritage cathedrals, spice plantations, and vibrant coastal culture.
history: Anciently ruled by the Bhojas, Kadambas of Goa, and Vijayanagara Empire. Conquered in 1510 by Afonso de Albuquerque, initiating four and a half centuries of Portuguese rule until liberated by the Indian Armed Forces in Operation Vijay on 19 December 1961.
geography: Part of the Konkan coastal strip, backed by the biodiversity-rich Western Ghats (Sahyadris) in the east, drained by the Mandovi, Zuari, and Chapora rivers.
climate: Tropical maritime climate. Summers (March to May) are warm and humid (26°C - 34°C). The southwest monsoon douses the state from June to September. Winters (November to February) are pleasant and breezy (20°C - 31°C).

historical_timeline.title: Kadambas of Goa
historical_timeline.description: Kadamba dynasty established Chandor and Gopakapattana as bustling maritime trading capitals.
historical_timeline.significance: Early flourishing of Goan seafaring commerce and classical temple architecture.

historical_timeline.title: Portuguese Colonial Epoch
historical_timeline.description: Old Goa became the 'Rome of the East', headquarters of the Portuguese Estado da India.
historical_timeline.significance: Construction of UNESCO Basilica of Bom Jesus, Se Cathedral, and Latin Quarter urbanism.

historical_timeline.title: Operation Vijay & Liberation
historical_timeline.description: Indian Armed Forces integrated Goa, Daman, and Diu into the Indian Union.
historical_timeline.significance: Attainment of freedom and subsequent full statehood in 1987.

travel_transport.connectivity_tip: Two international airports provide convenient access to both North and South Goa resort belts.

destinations.name: Old Goa (Velha Goa)
destinations.description: UNESCO World Heritage precinct preserving majestic 16th-century Manueline and Baroque cathedrals.
destinations.why_famous: Basilica of Bom Jesus housing the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier, and the imposing Se Cathedral with the Golden Bell.
highlights: Church of St. Francis of Assisi

destinations.name: Palolem Beach
destinations.description: Crescent-shaped paradise beach in South Goa sheltered by palm headlands, celebrated for calm turquoise swimming waters.
destinations.why_famous: Tranquil beach huts, kayaking, dolphin spotting tours, and serene sunset views.

destinations.name: Dudhsagar Falls
destinations.description: Spectacular four-tiered 310m waterfall on the Mandovi River deep inside Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary.
destinations.why_famous: One of India's tallest waterfalls where the railway track crosses dramatically across the white foaming cascade.

name: Gujarat
description: The Land of Legends, birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Boasting India's longest coastline (1,600 km), the gleaming white salt desert of the Rann of Kutch, the sole wild habitat of the Asiatic Lion in Gir, and the world's tallest monument: the Statue of Unity.
history: Home to maritime Indus Valley cities of Lothal (world's oldest dockyard) and Dholavira (UNESCO). Ruled by the Solankis who built the Sun Temple of Modhera and Rani ki Vav stepwell. Pivotal in the Indian freedom struggle through Gandhi's Sabarmati Ashram and the 1930 Dandi Salt March.
geography: Highly diverse: the Thar desert margin and white salt flats in Kutch, the peninsular Saurashtra plateau with Gir hill forests, and fertile alluvial plains along the Narmada, Tapi, and Sabarmati rivers.
climate: Arid to semi-arid in Kutch and north Gujarat; sub-humid in the south. Blistering summers (March to June, up to 43°C); brief monsoons; delightful, crisp winters (November to February, 12°C - 28°C) perfect for Rann Utsav.

historical_timeline.title: Indus Valley Maritime Port of Lothal
historical_timeline.description: Engineered the world's earliest known tidal dockyard connecting trade to Mesopotamia and Egypt.
historical_timeline.significance: UNESCO-recognized pinnacle of proto-historic hydraulic engineering and bead trade.

historical_timeline.title: Rani ki Vav Stepwell Commissioning
historical_timeline.description: Queen Udayamati commissioned the inverted temple stepwell in memory of King Bhima I.
historical_timeline.significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 500 principal sculptures representing the Solanki style.

historical_timeline.title: Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi March
historical_timeline.description: Gandhi marched 390 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to defy the British salt tax.
historical_timeline.significance: Sparked nationwide civil disobedience that shook the foundations of the British Empire.

festivals: Navratri (9 nights of Garba dance - UNESCO Intangible)

airports: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad (AMD)
travel_transport.connectivity_tip: Vande Bharat Express links Ahmedabad and Mumbai in under 5 hours 15 minutes.

destinations.name: Statue of Unity (Kevadia)
destinations.description: The world's tallest statue (182 meters) honoring Iron Man of India Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, set along the scenic Narmada river.
destinations.why_famous: Viewing gallery at 153 meters inside the chest, high-speed elevators, Valley of Flowers, and Glow Garden.

destinations.name: Rann of Kutch
destinations.description: Massive seasonal salt marsh that transforms into an ethereal endless white desert under the full moon during the annual Rann Utsav.
destinations.why_famous: Full moon night walks over blinding white salt crystals, traditional Kutchi tent cities, and desert camel safaris.

destinations.name: Gir National Park
destinations.description: The sole sanctuary on the planet where the Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) roams freely in the wild.
destinations.why_famous: Jeep safaris through dry deciduous teak forest hosting over 670 wild Asiatic lions, leopards, and 300+ bird species.

name: Haryana
description: The cradle of Vedic civilization where the timeless philosophy of the Bhagavad Gita was delivered by Lord Krishna at Kurukshetra. Haryana combines ancient archaeological heritage (Rakhigarhi) with modern technological hubs like Gurugram.
history: Anciently home to the Saraswati river valley civilization and the epic Mahabharata battle at Kurukshetra. The plains of Panipat witnessed three historic battles that repeatedly reshaped the destiny of India (1526, 1556, 1761).
geography: Predominantly flat alluvial plains of the Yamuna-Ghaggar basin, bounded by the Shivalik hill range in the northeast (Morni Hills) and the dry Aravalli outcrops in the south.
climate: Continental semi-arid climate with sharp seasonal swings: scorching summers (April to June, up to 44°C) and crisp cold winters (December to February, 3°C - 20°C).

historical_timeline.title: Indus Valley Metropolis of Rakhigarhi
historical_timeline.description: Excavations revealed Rakhigarhi as the largest Harappan city site in the subcontinent.
historical_timeline.significance: Advanced drainage, planned brick streets, and DNA research tracing continuous ancestry.

historical_timeline.title: The Mahabharata at Kurukshetra
historical_timeline.description: Lord Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita to warrior Arjuna on the battlefield of Jyotisar.
historical_timeline.significance: Foundational text of Indian spiritual and philosophical thought.

historical_timeline.title: The Three Historic Battles of Panipat
historical_timeline.description: Decisive military confrontations that established the Mughal Empire, reaffirmed Akbar's rule, and shaped Maratha-Afghan geopolitics.
historical_timeline.significance: Turning points in early modern subcontinental history.

local_cuisine: Bajre ki Roti with White Butter

airports: Served directly by Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi (DEL)
travel_transport.connectivity_tip: Metro networks (Delhi Metro & Rapid Metro) connect Gurugram and Faridabad directly to central Delhi.

destinations.name: Kurukshetra
destinations.description: Sacred historical city where the Mahabharata war was fought and Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita.
destinations.why_famous: Brahma Sarovar (massive sacred water reservoir), Jyotisar (under the immortal Banyan tree), and the Panorama Science Centre.

destinations.name: Sultanpur National Park
destinations.description: Ramsar wetland bird paradise located just outside Gurugram, hosting over 250 species of resident and migratory waterfowl.
destinations.why_famous: Winter haven for Siberian cranes, flamingos, bar-headed geese, and pelicans with dedicated observation towers.
